text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- A plan to introduce flexible workhours in Austria's metal industry fell through, due to the union's refusal to agree to employers' requests.
- Raiffeisenbank's Vienna unit has been taken over by Raiffeisen Landesbank of Lower Austria. The merger should be completed by autumn.

- The construction industry is demanding the newly introduced motorway fee be raised to 1,000 schillings annually. It says the government's plans to introduce a road pricing system for Austria's motorways should not be scrapped, as further road construction and maintenance could not be financed otherwise.
- Cartonmaker Mayr-Melnhof's pre-tax profits rose to 699 million schillings in 1996 from 430 million schillings a year ago. The company plans further expansion in Asia.
DIE PRESSE
- Ahead of the Social Democrat convention party members demand changes in the party's social and employment policies.
- Austria's state health insurance deficit sank to 386 million schillings in 1996 from 2,160 million the previous year due to an increase of fees.
- Real Estate firm Immorent will pay its parent GiroCredit 150 million schillings in dividends as profits grew in 1996.
- Papermaker Frantschach plans to take over Poland's number one cellulose-producer as the company sees improvement in 1997.
KURIER

- The government plans to include illegal work income in the calculation of gross domestic product. This way the Maastricht deficit criteria will be easily reached. Economic research institute Wifo says illegal work income accounts for up to 120 billion schillings.

- The sale of postal savings bank PSK to insurers BARC and Wiener Staedtische is not yet certain, as the two other bidders for the state's stake in the bank, BAWAG and GiroCredit, have not yet given up hope of a successful bid.
- Austria's builders see no end to the poor economic state of the industry as orders remain low. The government is criticised for being ineffective.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN

- Alfred Reiter will become the next chief executive of PSK, while Gerhard Praschak will become his successor at Investkredit. Former Transport Minister Rudolf Scholten will become head of the Kontrollbank.
- Austrian communities will be able to reduce their deficit to 0.3 percent of GDP in order to comply with the Maastricht criteria as pilot projects to farm out operations have been successful.
- Austria's economic growth was the second lowest in the European Union at one percent in 1996.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- OMV plans to participate in provincial gas provider Begas by buying a 49 percent stake in regional holding company Gemeindeanteilsverwaltung AG.
